problem: Existing reviews of embodied AI either cover only pure NLP/vision large models, are too broad (hardware + software), predate recent advances, or cover only one segment (e.g. manipulation) and skip navigation, so no full-stack review of multimodal large models for embodied agents exists.
motivation: Large models are rapidly being integrated into embodied agents for perception, navigation, interaction and simulation, but the field is fragmented across tasks, datasets and simulators. A systematic review is needed to map the technical roadmap, data resources and open challenges.
key_idea: A full-stack survey of Embodied Multimodal Large Models (EMLMs) organized by foundation models, embodied perception, navigation, interaction, simulation and datasets, followed by challenges and future directions.
insight: The survey groups navigation methods into general LLM/LVLM-based (LM-Nav, NavGPT, SG-Nav, VLFM) versus specialized trained models (NaviLLM, NavCoT, NavGPT-2, GNM/ViNT/NoMaD). It finds that current models are task-specific with limited generalization, that datasets focus on manipulation and rely mainly on cameras, and that long-horizon continuous navigation models are lacking. It is a literature review with no experiments or ablations, so these conclusions are qualitative.
method: Foundation models: reviews LLMs (GPT, BERT, T5, LLaMA), LVMs (ResNet, ViT, Swin, SAM, DINOv2), LVLMs (CLIP, BLIP, Flamingo, PaLM-E), plus audio and touch models.
Embodied perception: splits into GPT-based (Octopus, CoPa, AlphaBlock, VoxPoser, ReKep, RobotGPT) and non-GPT models (PaLM-E, RT-1/2/H, RoboFlamingo, OpenVLA, RoboMamba), with a comparison table.
Embodied navigation: splits into general large models (LM-Nav, L3MVN, LFG, VLMaps, NavGPT, SG-Nav, CLIP/BLIP-based VLFM) and specialized models (NavCoT, NaviLLM, NavGPT-2, GOAT, VER, GNM/ViNT/NoMaD).
Embodied interaction: separates short-horizon action policies (R3M, RT-1, Octo, VIMA, OpenVLA, GR-1) from long-horizon planners (SayCan, Text2Motion, EmbodiedGPT, LEO, SayPlan).

Simulation and datasets: covers simulators (Isaac Sim, iGibson 2.0, Habitat-Sim, Genesis, SoundSpaces, etc.), data collection methods, and action datasets (Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, DROID) and navigation datasets (HM3D, Gibson, MP3D, R2R, REVERIE, RxR, CVDN).

Challenges and future directions: cross-modal alignment, compute efficiency, generalization, temporal reasoning, dataset diversity, ethics; proposes self-supervised learning, multimodal RL and end-to-end models.
numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results of its own. Tables list model architecture, platform and dataset, not performance metrics.
results: This is the first claimed systematic review of EMLMs, covering about 300 papers across perception, navigation, interaction, simulation and datasets. It reports no benchmark numbers. Its main findings are that generalization, cross-modal alignment, compute cost, and the lack of diverse multi-sensor data and long-horizon navigation models are the key open problems.
limitations: Descriptive review with no unified quantitative comparison of methods.

Navigation coverage is relatively shallow: VLN and ObjectNav methods are listed without benchmark results, and some entries contain citation or attribution errors (e.g. Trans-EQA attributed to DiscussNav).
Emphasis on manipulation datasets, with limited analysis of navigation datasets and simulators.
